note: Element pages of the Chip Explorer (/explorer/element/). Layout / timing / clock / RTL data (data/<id>.json, .cells.bin, .clk.bin, .rtl.json) is written by tools/explorer_elem_export.py into the fleet-viz deploy dir, not committed. The per-element prose below (function, algorithm summary with RTL line links, bench provenance, design-intent rates) is written by hand from the RTL at the closure's source commit; every line reference is to that commit.

pages.title: BF element: hierarchical column vs flat half-rate
pages.summary: Two routed versions of the BF weight-multiply element: the flat half-rate pair that closed first and one column of the hierarchical full-rate design the owner adopted, each from its final routed database and its RTL at the closure's source commit.

bf_col600.function: Takes the activation slice the front block issues — two 256-bit FP8/FP4 halves with their 10-bit exponents (i2x_q0/i2x_e0, i2x_q1/i2x_e1), the 17-bit issue tag (i1_t) and the per-segment row/index tables (so_row, so_idx, so_n) — and multiplies it by weights read from the column's own two 4096 × 274 ROMs. It emits one FP32 partial dot product per segment and position (pval, 32 bit) with its row (prow), segment (pseg, pnseg), position (ppos) and error flag. Each cycle the column consumes one 274-bit weight word: 32 FP8 or 64 FP4 weights with a shared power-of-two scale, or 16 BF16 weights.

summary.t: Register every input at the column boundary on the free clock (one cycle), including the gate enable and reset.
Read one 274-bit weight word per cycle from two ROMs used alternately (ping-pong, each read a 2-cycle path); capture it at the macro pins.
FP8/FP4: two lane units each form one 32-product block dot exactly, round it once to FP32 (RNE), then scale by 2^(x exponent + weight exponent).
Accumulate a unit's 8 block terms in issue order, one FP32 RNE add per term (two chains, one per lane unit).
FP4: add the two sibling chunks (pair adder); FP8: both chunks go to the tree as separate nodes.
BF16: 16 lanes each multiply and sequentially add 8 products, then a pairwise tree combines the lanes.
Pairwise FP32 tree over the segment's nodes (zero-padded to a power of two), early exit when the segment is complete.
Output registers: the tree result with its row, segment, count and position tags; idle halves emit nothing.

bf_halfphl.function: Takes the BF pair's pins — configuration writes (cfg_v/cfg_a/cfg_d), go/go_bf, the 256-bit FP8/FP4 activation halves with exponents (xs_q0/xs_e0, xs_q1/xs_e1) and the 1,024-bit BF16 activation block (xb_d) with their positions — and multiplies them by weights read from four 4096 × 274 ROMs (two per MAC). It emits two FP32 partial dot products, one per MAC, per segment and position (pval, 2 × 32 bit) with row, segment, position and error tags, plus busy/fault and the half-rate phase (hph). The element's registers are clocked every other cycle, so each MAC consumes one 274-bit weight word every two clock cycles.

summary.t: Capture every pin in a register on the clock (pin registers).
Generate the half-rate element clock: a phase flop toggles every cycle and gates the clock (eclk), so the element runs on every other edge; a second toggle on eclk proves the phase each cycle.
Inside the element, register the issued activations, then fan them to the two MACs.
Per MAC: read one weight word from two ROMs used alternately (ping-pong).
FP8/FP4: two lane units form 32-product block dots exactly, round once to FP32 and scale by the two exponents.
Accumulate 8 block terms per chain in order (FP32 RNE), pair FP4 chunks, BF16 lanes multiply-accumulate then tree.
Pairwise FP32 segment tree, then the MAC's output registers.
Re-time outputs to the full-rate clock: valid only in the cycle after the slow edge.
